definitions.explanation: A combining form used in the names of Japan's education-and-science ministry and its minister: {文部科学省|もんぶかがくしょう} (MEXT) and {文部科学大臣|もんぶかがくだいじん} (Minister of Education). Almost never used alone.

examples.japanese: {文部科学省|もんぶかがくしょう}が{発表|はっぴょう}した。
{文部科学大臣|もんぶかがくだいじん}が{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: The Minister of Education held a press conference.

examples.japanese: この{奨学金|しょうがくきん}は{文部科学省|もんぶかがくしょう}の{支援|しえん}を{受|う}けている。
examples.english: This scholarship is supported by the Ministry of Education.

notes:
A fixed combining element formed from {文部|もんぶ} (literary/educational affairs) + {科学|かがく} (science). It is not used on its own — only as a prefix in fixed ministry-related compounds.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {文部科学省|もんぶかがくしょう}: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
- {文部科学大臣|もんぶかがくだいじん}: Minister of Education
- {文部科学省告示|もんぶかがくしょうこくじ}: MEXT public notice

BACKGROUND:
Formed in 2001 when the former Ministry of Education ({文部省|もんぶしょう}) merged with the Science and Technology Agency. The merged portfolio covers schools, universities, sports, culture, and science policy.
